text: Edward Ambrose Hug (July 14, 1880 – May 11, 1953) was an American Major League Baseball catcher who played in one game for the Brooklyn Superbas in 1903. His only Major League appearance occurred on July 6 in the second game of a doubleheader in Cincinnati, where he relieved a fatigued Lew Ritter in the fifth inning as a local amateur catcher. During his plate appearance, he walked. The game was called in the seventh inning to allow the Brooklyn team to catch their train out of town. Hug shares the major league records for the shortest name and the shortest career. He is buried at New St. Joseph Cemetery in Cincinnati.
